pluss::note::from_words¶

Back to Note Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Note pluss::note::from_words(string_view text)

Split One String Into A Column Of Whitespace-Separated Tokens¶

from_words() takes a single string and returns a rank-1 Note with one cell per whitespace-delimited run of non-space characters. It is the quick path from a sentence, a command line, or a space-separated record to an addressable token column.

Separators are ASCII whitespace — space, tab (\t), newline (\n), carriage return (\r), vertical tab, and form feed. Any run of one or more of these characters is a single separator, so consecutive spaces, leading whitespace, and trailing whitespace never produce empty cells. This is the “split on whitespace” behavior of most scripting languages, not a fixed single-delimiter split.

The result is always rank 1 and UTF-8 mode. Tokens are taken as raw byte spans between separators, so multi-byte UTF-8 characters inside a token are preserved; only ASCII whitespace ends a token. An input that is empty or all whitespace yields a zero-length Note.

from_words does no punctuation handling — "end." is one token including the period. Strip or split punctuation with Note methods afterward if you need bare words.

Example 1: A Sentence With Irregular Spacing¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::from_words("  the   quick brown  "))
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["the", "quick", "brown"]

Leading, trailing, and doubled spaces all collapse; no empty cells.

Example 2: Mixed Whitespace Kinds¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::from_words("tab\tand\nnewline");
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["tab", "and", "newline"]

Tabs and newlines separate tokens just as spaces do.

Example 3: A Single Token¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout, pluss::note::from_words("single")) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["single"]

Still a rank-1 Note — one cell, not a scalar.

Example 4: Only Whitespace¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::from_words("   ")) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]

No tokens, so a zero-length Note.

See Also¶

  • pluss::note::from_lines: split on line breaks instead of on whitespace runs.

  • pluss::note::perm: generate character selections of a word rather than reading words from text.

  • pluss::note::make: build a column from tokens you already hold separately.
